acceptance: Two fixture lanes that each remove one copy merge to a green main without a conflict on go/.test-dup-baseline
A new copy still fails the ratchet
go/acs/cycle2231 predicates stay green, or a documented retire step replaces the ones the design changes
fix: Design first: compare the options (a) count at most the baseline, and a boundary tighten step lowers the baseline, as the size ratchet does; (b) a per-change rule that judges only the copies a change adds against its base. Keep the frozen predicates of go/acs/cycle2231 green, because they pin the equal-count rule (TestC2231_003).
summary: Check in go/internal/testdup fails when the count is below the baseline, so a lane that removes a copy must lower go/.test-dup-baseline in the same commit. Two lanes in one wave that each remove one copy both write the same line: the second rebase conflicts, or the merged tree is one below the baseline and red. See docs/incidents/2026-11-09-duplicate-ratchet-misses-staged-predicates.md (Limits).
title: The duplicate ratchet's equal-count rule makes concurrent lanes that each remove a copy conflict on go/.test-dup-baseline
